name: Finasteride
mechanism_summary: Inhibits the Type II 5 alpha-reductase enzyme blocking conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone (DHT). Over time this results in the shrinking of the prostate and improvement in urinary flow. indications: Treatment, as monotherapy , of symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) in men with an enlarged prostate to: Improve symptoms Reduce the risk of acute urinary retention Reduce the risk of the need for BPH-related surgery; Treatment, in combination with the alpha-blocker, doxazosin, to reduce the risk of symptomatic progression of BPH; Treatment of male pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia) in men only
contraindications: Women who are pregnant or who have potential to become pregnant; Hypersensitivity to finasteride or any formulation ingredients

name: Sildenafil
mechanism_summary: Inhibits cGMP specific phosphodiesterase type-5 (PDE-5) enzymes from degrading cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) . Sexual stimulation creates a release of nitric oxide, which increases cGMP that causes smooth muscle relaxation allowing blood flow into the penis to produce an erection. This same effect in the pulmonary vascular bed leads to vasodilation for the treatment of pulmonary arterial hypertension.
indications: Treatment of erectile dysfunction; Treatment of pulmonary arterial hypertension (WHO group I) in adults to improve exercise ability and delay clinical worsening; efficacy established predominately in patients with NYHA functional class II and III symptoms and idiopathic etiology (71%) or associated with connective tissue disease (CTD) (25%)
contraindications: Regular or intermittent use of organic nitrates or nitrites in any form (e.g. nitroglycerin, isosorbide); Concomitant use of a guanylate cyclase stimulator (e.g. riociguat); Hypersensitivity to sildenafil or any formulation ingredients

contraindications: Regular or intermittent use of organic nitrates or nitrites in any form (e.g. nitroglycerin, isosorbide); Concomitant use of a guanylate cyclase stimulator (e.g. riociguat); Hypersensitivity to tadalafil or any formulation ingredients

mechanism_summary: Inhibits cGMP specific phosphodiesterase type-5 (PDE-5) enzymes from degrading cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) . Sexual stimulation creates a release of nitric oxide, which increases cGMP that causes smooth muscle relaxation allowing blood flow into the penis to produce an erection.
indications: Treatment of erectile dysfunction
contraindications: Regular or intermittent use of organic nitrates or nitrites in any form (e.g. nitroglycerin, isosorbide); In a patient who has taken avanafil, where nitrate administration is deemed medically necessary in a life-threatening situation, at least 12 hours should elapse after the last dose of avanafil before nitrate administration is considered. name: Allopurinol
mechanism_summary: Inhibits xanthine oxidase , thus reducing uric acid production. Xanthine oxidase is the enzyme responsible for the conversion of hypoxanthine to xanthine and of xanthine to uric acid.
indications: Treatment of gout : management of signs and symptoms of primary or secondary gout (acute attacks, tophi, joint destruction, uric acid lithiasis, and/or nephropathy).; Prevention of tumor lysis syndrome : management of patients with leukemia, lymphoma and malignancies who are receiving cancer therapy which causes elevations of serum and urinary uric acid levels. Treatment with allopurinol should be discontinued when the potential for overproduction of uric acid is no longer present.; Prevention of recurrent calcium kidney stones (nephrolithiasis) : management of patients with recurrent calcium oxalate calculi whose daily uric acid excretion exceeds 800 mg/day in male patients and 750 mg/day in female patients. Therapy in such patients should be carefully assessed initially and reassessed periodically to determine in each case that treatment is beneficial and that the benefits outweigh the risks.
contraindications: Those with history of severe reaction to allopurinol should not be restarted on the drug; Hypersensitivity to any formulation ingredients

name: Nitrofurantoin
mechanism_summary: Nitrofurantoin is reduced by bacterial flavoproteins to reactive intermediates which inactivate or alter bacterial ribosomal proteins and other macromolecules. As a result of such inactivations, the vital biochemical processes of protein synthesis, aerobic energy metabolism, DNA synthesis, RNA synthesis, and cell wall synthesis are inhibited.

contraindications: Anuria, oliguria, or significant impairment of renal function (CrCl <60 mL/min* or clinically significant elevated serum creatinine) *Some literature supports use in lower renal function; History of cholestatic jaundice/hepatic dysfunction associated with nitrofurantoin; Hypersensitivity to nitrofurantoin or any formulation ingredients; Because of the possibility of hemolytic anemia caused by immature erythrocyte enzyme systems (glutathione instability), the drug is contraindicated in pregnant patients at term (38 to 42 weeks gestation), during labor and delivery, or when the onset of labor is imminent; also contraindicated in neonates younger than 1 month of age

name: Clindamycin
mechanism_summary: Reversibly binds to the 50S subunit of bacterial ribosomes inhibiting protein synthesis .
indications: Treatment of serious infections caused by susceptible strains of anaerobic, streptococci, pneumococci , and staphylococci bacteria. Use should be reserved for penicillin-allergic patients or other patients for whom, in the judgment of the healthcare provider, a penicillin is inappropriate. Streptococci: Serious respiratory tract infections; serious skin and soft tissue infections. Staphylococci: Serious respiratory tract infections; serious skin and soft tissue infections. Pneumococci: Serious respiratory tract infections. Bacteriologic studies should be performed to determine the causative organisms and their susceptibility to clindamycin.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to clindamycin, lincomycin, or any formulation ingredients

Its diuretic/antihypertensive action is caused by competitive binding of receptors at the aldosterone-dependent sodium-potassium exchange site in the distal convoluted renal tubule, which results in increased sodium and water excretion and potassium retention . name: Combined Oral Contraceptive
mechanism_summary: Combined oral contraceptives (COCs) prevent pregnancy by inhibiting ovulation , interfering with sperm travel through the cervix, and disrupting implantation of fertilized eggs in the uterus. The progestin component prevents the pre-ovulation surge of luteinizing hormone (LH), which decreases the likelihood that ovulation will occur. The progestin also thickens cervical mucus, inhibiting the ability of sperm to travel into the uterus, and thins the endometrium (lining of the uterus), making implantation of a fertilized egg more difficult. Estrogen additionally prevents ovulation by inhibiting LH further and inhibiting the release of follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), which disrupts the maturation of ovarian follicles that release eggs.

These uses vary by product and are often off-label ; refer to clinical guidelines and manufacturer labeling for product specific uses. Examples of noncontraceptive uses for COCs include: Acne (moderate to severe) Bone health Dysmenorrhea (menstrual cramps) Endometriosis (painful, excess uterine tissue growth) Endometrial cancer risk reduction in those with increased risk Hirsutism (excess, male-pattern hair growth) Hormone replacement in women with primary hypogonadism or premature ovarian insufficiency Menorrhagia (heavy menstrual bleeding) and associated anemia Perimenopausal symptoms (hot flashes, night sweats) Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS), regulating menses and other symptoms Premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) Ovarian cyst prevention (does not treat existing cysts)

If implantation has already occurred, ulipristal will have no effect on stopping pregnancy.

Structurally, cyclobenzaprine is similar to tricyclic antidepressants and also produces anticholinergic effects.

name: Digoxin
mechanism_summary: Digoxin inhibits the sodium potassium adenosine triphosphatase (Na/K-ATPase) pump , thereby increasing intracellular calcium and enhancing cardiac contractility. It also acts directly on the atrioventricular node (AV node), suppressing conduction velocity. Likely due to its effects on intracellular calcium concentrations, digoxin induces apoptosis of tumor cells via a pathway involving mitochondrial cytochrome c and caspases 8 and 3.
indications: Atrial fibrillation or atrial flutter; for rate control: control of ventricular response rate in adult patients with chronic atrial fibrillation; Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF): treatment of mild to moderate (ACCF/AHA stage C) heart failure in adults ; and to increase myocardial contractility in pediatric patients with heart failure
contraindications: Ventricular fibrillation; Known hypersensitivity to digoxin, other digitalis preparations, or any formulation ingredients

name: Amiodarone
mechanism_summary: Amiodarone primarily blocks myocardial potassium channels , in addition to blocking calcium and sodium channels in cardiac tissue, resulting in prolongation of the cardiac action potential and refractory period. Amiodarone also inhibits alpha- and beta-adrenergic receptors, resulting in a reduction in sympathetic stimulation of the heart, a negative chronotropic effect, and a decrease in myocardial oxygen demands. Amiodarone may cause vasodilation by stimulation of the release of nitric oxide and cyclooxygenase-dependent relaxing endothelial factors.
indications: Ventricular arrhythmias: treatment of documented, life-threatening recurrent ventricular fibrillation and life-threatening recurrent hemodynamically unstable tachycardia in adults who have not responded to adequate doses of other available antiarrhythmics or when alternative agents cannot be tolerated
contraindications: Cardiogenic shock; Sick sinus syndrome, second- or third-degree atrioventricular block, bradycardia leading to syncope without a functioning pacemaker; Known hypersensitivity to amiodarone or any formulation ingredients, including iodine

name: Meclizine
mechanism_summary: Meclizine is a synthetic piperazine with anti-emetic, sedative and histamine-H1 antagonistic properties. Meclizine blocks H1 histamine receptors and prevents the symptoms that are caused by histamine activity on capillaries, bronchial and gastrointestinal smooth muscles, including vasodilation, increased capillary permeability, bronchoconstriction, and spasmodic contraction of gastrointestinal smooth muscles. Meclizine may exert its antiemetic effects by its anticholinergic actions or due to a direct effect on the medullary chemoreceptive trigger zone.
indications: Treatment of vertigo associated with diseases affecting the vestibular system in adults; Prevention and treatment of nausea, vomiting, and/or dizziness associated with motion sickness

name: Armodafinil
mechanism_summary: The mechanism(s) through which armodafinil promotes wakefulness is unknown . Armodafinil (R-modafinil) has pharmacological properties similar to those of modafinil (a mixture of R- and S-modafinil). In vitro, modafinil binds to the dopamine transporter and inhibits dopamine reuptake . In genetically engineered mice lacking the dopamine transporter, modafinil lacked wake-promoting activity. However, the wake-promoting effects of modafinil were not antagonized by the dopamine receptor antagonist haloperidol in rats.
